newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via multi-day system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via multi-day system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to inject reserves into the banking system through a round of system repurchase agreements Monday, analysts said.
The RPs would either be three-, four-, or seven day, analysts predicted.
The average daily add need for the first week of the two-week maintenance period, ending Wednesday, is seen about $6 billion.
"To address this need the Fed will likely execute a three- day system repo, or even a four-day system repo, which would cover the Thanksgiving holiday," said UBS Securities analysts.
Others, though, see the Fed taking care of the add need for the whole week.
Reserve pressures are minimal Monday, with the Fed funds rate only slightly above target at 5-5/16 percent.
The Fed added Friday via $2 billion customer RPs.

Analysts still look for the Fed to add permanent reserves to the banking system through an outright purchase of coupons, as currency in circulation rises during the holiday period. But the coupon pass isn't expected until after Thanksgiving.
